name: @whoisxmlapidotcom/mcp-whoisxmlapi

tools.name: brand_alert
tools.description: Find newly added, dropped, or updated domains whose names contain specified brand terms. Use this for typosquat detection, lookalike-domain detection, and brand-protection workflows. Do NOT use this for matching against WHOIS contact fields (use `registrant_alert`) or for general WHOIS-text matching (use `reverse_whois`). Set with_typos=true to automatically expand brand terms with common typo variants.

date.description: Date to query in YYYY-MM-DD format. When omitted, the upstream API uses its own default (typically yesterday).

excluded_search_terms.description: Comma-separated terms to exclude. Max 4 items.

included_search_terms.description: Comma-separated brand terms to include (AND logic). Max 4 items. Case insensitive. Wildcards * supported.

mode.description: 'preview' returns count only (no credits used). 'purchase' returns the full domain list.

punycode.description: If true, encodes domain names to Punycode.

with_typos.description: If true, includes typo variations of brand terms (transposed letters, homoglyphs, missing chars, etc.).

tools.name: bulk_dns_lookup
tools.description: Run DNS lookups for up to 200 domains in a single call. Emulated bulk (no native upstream endpoint): the server fans out single lookups concurrently and returns a unified envelope, 1 credit per input. Use this whenever you have ≥2 domains and want concurrent execution under one rate-limit budget. For >200 inputs, split client-side. Do NOT use this for historical DNS records (use `dns_history`) or for a single domain (use `dns_lookup` directly).

domain_names.description: Domain names to look up (1 credit per domain, max 200 per call).

query_type.description: Comma-separated DNS query types (A, MX, NS, SOA, etc.) or "all". Applied uniformly to all inputs.

tools.name: bulk_email_verification
tools.description: Run email verification for up to 10,000 addresses in a single call. Native bulk via WhoisXML's Bulk Email Verification API; 1 credit per email. Returns inline if it completes within 20s, otherwise returns a `job_id` to poll via `bulk_job_status` / `bulk_job_results`. Use this for lead-list hygiene at any scale ≥2 emails. Do NOT use this for live polling of an in-flight job (use `bulk_job_status` for status, `bulk_job_results` to fetch completed rows) or for a single email (use `email_verification`).

emails.description: Email addresses to verify (1 credit per email, max 10000 per call).

tools.name: bulk_ip_geolocation
tools.description: Run IP geolocation for up to 200 IP addresses in a single call. Emulated bulk (no native upstream endpoint exists; WhoisXML's bulk IP-geo product is CSV-only via web UI). Server fans out single lookups concurrently, 1 credit per input. Use this whenever you have ≥2 IPs to enrich. For >200 IPs, split client-side. Do NOT use this for ASN/CIDR ownership lookups (use `ip_netblocks`) or for a single IP (use `ipgeolocation` directly).

ip_addresses.description: IP addresses to look up (1 credit per IP, max 200 per call).

tools.name: bulk_job_results
tools.description: Fetch full per-input results for a completed native bulk job (created by `bulk_whois` or `bulk_email_verification`). If the job is still in flight, returns `status=running` with progress; the caller should retry. Per-input order may differ from the original input order. Do NOT use this for emulated bulk tools (`bulk_dns_lookup`, `bulk_subdomain_lookup`, `bulk_ip_geolocation`); they always return inline.

job_id.description: Opaque job identifier returned by a bulk_* tool when status=running.

tools.name: bulk_job_status
tools.description: Check progress of an in-flight bulk job created by `bulk_whois` or `bulk_email_verification`. Returns `running` or `completed` plus progress counters. Use this when a bulk call returned a `job_id` instead of inline results — poll until completed, then call `bulk_job_results`. Do NOT use this for emulated bulk tools (`bulk_dns_lookup`, `bulk_subdomain_lookup`, `bulk_ip_geolocation`); they always return inline.

job_id.description: Opaque job identifier returned by a bulk_* tool when status=running.

tools.name: bulk_subdomain_lookup
tools.description: Discover subdomains for up to 200 apex domains in a single call. Emulated bulk: fans out single subdomain lookups concurrently. Reuses the in-memory cache of `subdomain_lookup`, so re-querying recently-fetched domains is free; otherwise 1 credit per input. Use this for attack-surface mapping across an organisation's full apex-domain portfolio in one shot. Do NOT use this for domains or subdomains containing a search term (use `domain_and_subdomain_discovery`) or when you have a single apex (use `subdomain_lookup`).

domain_names.description: Domain names to look up (1 credit per uncached domain, max 200 per call).

tools.name: bulk_vpn_proxy_detection
tools.description: Check up to 100 IP addresses in one call for VPN, proxy, Tor exit, relay, hosting or CDN membership, using the VPN & Proxy Detection API's native batch endpoint. Requires a Starter or higher VPN & Proxy Detection plan. Rows carry the same fields as `vpn_proxy_detection` under the same plan rules: confidence, seen times and residential-proxy network names need Pro or higher, null below, and a residential-proxy network is named only where its exit is attributed. Rejected inputs, such as reserved addresses, come back as ok=false rows with an error code. Data is IPv4-first; IPv6 mostly returns unknown. Duplicates are looked up once. Costs 1 VPN & Proxy Detection API credit per IP successfully looked up; rejected rows are not charged. Use this whenever you have 2 or more IPs; split lists longer than 100 client-side.

ip_addresses.description: IP addresses to classify (max 100 per call; 1 credit per IP successfully looked up).

tools.name: bulk_whois
tools.description: Run WHOIS lookups for up to 10,000 domains in a single call. Native bulk via WhoisXML's Bulk WHOIS API; 1 credit per domain. Returns inline if it completes within 20s, otherwise returns a `job_id` to poll via `bulk_job_status` / `bulk_job_results`. Use this whenever you have ≥2 domains to look up — looping `whois` is strictly worse on rate-limit budget. Do NOT use this for live polling of an in-flight job (use `bulk_job_status` for status, `bulk_job_results` to fetch completed rows).

domains.description: Domain names to look up (1 credit per domain, max 10000 per call).

tools.name: categorization
tools.description: Classify a domain into IAB Content Taxonomy v3.1 content categories (Website Categorization v4). Returns 1-3 ranked categories plus a primary_category shortcut, each with a string ID (e.g. "IAB-596"), a human-readable hierarchical path ("Shopping > Online Marketplace") with tier1..tier4 levels, and a confidence score; response metadata includes taxonomy_version, credits_charged, latency_ms, model, an abstain object (flags parked/dead/thin sites with no real business purpose), a source object (is_historical_fallback marks results served from historical data when the live crawl was blocked), and error. Use this for content filtering, brand-safety gating, or to understand what a flagged domain claims to be. Do NOT use this for malware/phishing reputation (use `threat_intelligence` or `domain_reputation`) or for WHOIS/DNS facts (use `whois` / `dns_lookup`); unlike the legacy v3 API the response carries no ASN or domain-age data (use `ip_netblocks` / `whois` for those).

url.description: Full URL to classify (optional). Defaults upstream to https://{domain}; set it to categorize a specific page rather than the domain root.

tools.name: disposable_email_check
tools.description: Check whether an email address belongs to a disposable or temporary provider (e.g., mailinator, 10minutemail, guerrillamail). Returns a boolean verdict and the domain extracted from the address. Use this for lead-gen hygiene, signup-fraud filtering, or free-trial abuse detection when you only need the disposable verdict. Do NOT use this for full deliverability or mailbox-reachability checks — use `email_verification` instead.

tools.name: dns_history
tools.description: Look up historical DNS records for a domain (forward) or domains historically associated with an IP (reverse). Use this when investigating infrastructure pivots, domain takeovers, or when a current `dns_lookup` returns sparse/expired data. Do NOT use this for current resolution (use `dns_lookup`) or for the live set of domains on an IP right now (use `reverse_ip`).

domain_name.description: Required if "forward" search type. Domain name to search.

ip_address.description: Required if "reverse" search type. IP address to search. IPv4 returns A records, IPv6 returns AAAA records.

limit.description: Maximum records to return. Range: 1-1000. Recommended: 50.

record_type.description: DNS record type: "a" or "aaaa". Case insensitive.

tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: Resolve current DNS records for a domain — A, AAAA, MX, NS, SOA, TXT, CNAME, PTR, SRV, CAA, DS, DNSKEY, or `all`. Use this whenever you need today's authoritative answer for any record type. Do NOT use this for historical resolution data (use `dns_history`), to enumerate domains pointing at an IP (use `reverse_ip`), or to search records by pattern across the zone (use `reverse_dns`).

query_type.description: Comma-separated DNS query types (A, MX, NS, SOA, etc.) or "all".

tools.name: domain_and_subdomain_discovery
tools.description: Search WhoisXMLAPI's domain and subdomain index for names containing one or more search terms. Returns matching names whatever their age, not only recent registrations; pass `since` to narrow to names first seen after a date. Wildcards (`*`) supported; multiple terms combine with AND, so one call covers one apex-plus-term pair. Use this to sweep for typosquats and brand-impersonation hosts, including lookalikes on shared platforms that are subdomains carrying no registration of their own. Returns one page of at most 10000 names: while "truncated_at_upstream_cap" is true, call again with the response's "next_page_token"; if no token is present, stop and narrow the terms, as the result may be incomplete and cannot be continued. "domainsCount" is this page's size, NOT a total. Do NOT use this to enumerate the existing subdomain tree of a known domain (use `subdomain_lookup`) or for typosquat verification on an already-known domain (use `typosquatting`).

domain_search_terms.description: Comma-separated domain search terms (combined with AND logic). Max 4 items. Case insensitive. Must use wildcards for partial matches otherwise the search will be exact.

domain_search_terms_exclude.description: Comma-separated domain search terms to exclude. Max 4 items. Case insensitive.

next_page_token.description: IMPORTANT: To fetch the next page, copy the "next_page_token" value from the previous response and pass it here, with every other parameter unchanged. Do not use "search_after" or any other parameter name - only "next_page_token" is accepted.

since.description: Search domains/subdomains discovered since this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

subdomains_search_terms.description: Comma-separated subdomain search terms (combined with AND logic). Max 4 items. Case insensitive.

subdomains_search_terms_exclude.description: Comma-separated subdomain search terms to exclude. Max 4 items. Case insensitive.

tools.name: domain_info
tools.description: Get an enriched WHOIS profile for a domain by combining the current record with historical records to fill redacted or missing fields. Use this when a plain `whois` call returns redacted contacts or sparse data and you still need registrant/admin details. Do NOT use this for the historical timeline itself (use `whois_history`) or for a quick first-pass lookup where the current record is sufficient (use `whois`).

tools.name: domain_reputation
tools.description: Score a single domain's trustworthiness on a 0–100 scale by running live infrastructure and configuration checks (certificate validity, mail and name-server setup, malware-database and blackhole lookups, domain age, and more) and return the contributing test results with human-readable warnings. Use this to triage whether a flagged or unfamiliar domain is actually dangerous — for example after `typosquatting` or `brand_alert` surfaces a lookalike. Do NOT use it to look up a known-bad verdict from curated threat feeds (use `threat_intelligence`), to learn what a site claims to be (use `categorization`), or to fetch raw registration or zone records (those have their own dedicated lookup tools).

domain_name.description: Domain name to score (e.g., example.com). An IPv4 address is also accepted upstream.

mode.description: Depth of analysis. "fast" runs a select subset of checks (registration status, malware-database check, certificate validity) — cheaper, 1 credit. "full" runs every check (adds mail/name-server/SOA configuration, blackhole, certificate-vulnerability checks, and more) for a more complete score — heavier, 3 credits. Note the score is mode-dependent: "full" surfaces more warnings and so typically returns a LOWER score than "fast" for the same domain.

tools.name: email_verification
tools.description: Verify an email address via syntax check, MX lookup, and SMTP deliverability probe. Also flags disposable, role-based (e.g. `info@`, `noreply@`), free-provider, and catch-all addresses. Use this for lead-list hygiene or to gate signup forms. Do NOT use this to look up the registrant email of a domain (use `whois`) or when you have a list of >1 email (use `bulk_email_verification`).

tools.name: ip_netblocks
tools.description: Look up CIDR ranges, ASN number/name, organisation, and registration dates for an IP address, ASN, or organisation name. Use this when investigating who owns a chunk of address space or what netblocks an organisation controls. Do NOT use this for point-in-time geolocation of a single IP (use `ipgeolocation`) or to enumerate domains on the IP (use `reverse_ip`).

from_needle.description: Pagination needle from previous page's "inetnum" response.

ip_address.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address to search.

netmask_value.description: Netmask value: 0-32 for IPv4, 0-128 for IPv6.

tools.name: ipgeolocation
tools.description: Get geolocation data (country, region, city, ISP, ASN) for an IP address, domain, or email. Falls back to the caller's IP if no input is provided. Use this when assessing whether a connection or registration originates from an unexpected geography. Do NOT use this for IP netblock / ASN ownership queries (use `ip_netblocks`) or when you have many IPs to enrich (use `bulk_ip_geolocation`).

domain_name.description: Domain address. Cannot be used with ip_address or email_address.

email_address.description: Email address. Cannot be used with ip_address or domain_name.

ip_address.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address. Cannot be used with domain_name or email_address.

reverse_ip.description: If true, returns 5 domains associated with the IP address.

tools.name: registrant_alert
tools.description: Find newly added, dropped, or updated domains whose WHOIS records match search terms in registrant contact fields (email, name, organisation, etc.). Use this for brand-impersonation monitoring and threat-actor infrastructure tracking. Do NOT use this for general WHOIS-text matching (use `reverse_whois`) or for domain-name string matching.

date.description: Date to query in YYYY-MM-DD format. When omitted, the upstream API uses its own default (typically yesterday).

excluded_search_terms.description: Comma-separated terms to exclude. Max 4 items.

included_search_terms.description: Comma-separated terms to include (AND logic). Max 4 items. Case insensitive. Wildcards * supported.

mode.description: 'preview' returns count only (no credits used). 'purchase' returns the full domain list.

punycode.description: If true, encodes domain names to Punycode.

with_typos.description: If true, includes typo variations of search terms.

tools.name: reverse_dns
tools.description: Search across DNS records by pattern and return matching domains plus the record values. Multiple search terms combine with AND — use separate calls for OR. Wildcards (`*`) are required for partial matches; otherwise the search is exact. Use this when sweeping the zone for SPF strings, TXT verification tokens, or arbitrary RDATA patterns. Do NOT use this when you already know the domain (use `dns_lookup`) or when the input is an IP (use `reverse_ip`).

include_additional_checks.description: If true, performs wildcard and domain activeness checks. Extra cost.

limit.description: Maximum records to return. Recommended to start with 10 and increase if needed. Max: 1000.

preview.description: If true, returns just the domain names without additional information.

terms.description: Search terms array defining what to search for in DNS records (combined with AND logic). Must use wildcards for partial matches otherwise the search will be exact.

exclude.description: If true, excludes matching records from results.

tools.name: reverse_ip
tools.description: Find every domain currently pointing at a given IP address, with first-/last-seen dates per domain. Use this when investigating shared hosting, malicious infrastructure pivots, or to enumerate co-tenants of a flagged IP. Do NOT use this to resolve a domain's IP (use `dns_lookup`) or to search DNS records by pattern (use `reverse_dns`).

from_needle.description: Pagination needle from previous response. Max 300 records per page.

include_additional_checks.description: If true, performs additional DNS checks (wildcard, domain activeness). Slower but more detailed.

preview.description: If true, returns just the domain names without additional information.

tools.name: reverse_mx
tools.description: Find every domain that uses a specific MX server, with first-/last-seen dates. Use this when sweeping for domains that share a phishing-friendly mail provider, or to map an organisation's mail-handling fleet. Do NOT use this for nameservers (use `reverse_ns`) or for hosting IPs (use `reverse_ip`).

from_needle.description: Pagination needle from previous response. Max 300 records per page.

include_additional_checks.description: If true, performs wildcard and domain activeness checks. Extra cost.

preview.description: If true, returns just the domain names without additional information.

tools.name: reverse_ns
tools.description: Find every domain delegated to a specific authoritative nameserver, with first-/last-seen dates. Use this when an attacker uses a private NS infrastructure and you want to enumerate the rest of their fleet. Do NOT use this for MX servers (use `reverse_mx`) or hosting IPs (use `reverse_ip`).

from_needle.description: Pagination needle from previous response. Max 300 records per page.

include_additional_checks.description: If true, performs wildcard and domain activeness checks. Extra cost.

preview.description: If true, returns just the domain names without additional information.

tools.name: reverse_whois
tools.description: Find every domain whose WHOIS record contains a given free-text search term (registrant name, email, organisation, address, etc.). Wildcards (`*`) and partial matches supported; multiple terms combine with AND. Use this when pivoting from a known registrant identity to other domains they own. Do NOT use this when you need a field-targeted query (use `reverse_whois_advanced`) or when you only have the domain (use `whois` / `whois_history`).

count_only.description: If true, returns only count (no credit usage). If false, returns domain list.

created_date_from.description: Search domains created after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

created_date_to.description: Search domains created before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

excluded_search_terms.description: Comma-separated search terms to exclude. Max 4 items. Case insensitive.

include_audit_dates.description: If true, includes domain list and last audit date.

included_search_terms.description: Comma-separated search terms to include (combined with AND logic). Max 4 items. Case insensitive.

punycode.description: If true, encodes domain names to Punycode.

search_after.description: Pagination needle from previous page's "nextPageSearchAfter" value.

search_type.description: Search type: "current" or "historic". "current" searches current records, "historic" searches all records.

updated_date_from.description: Search domains updated after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

updated_date_to.description: Search domains updated before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: reverse_whois_advanced
tools.description: Find domains using field-specific WHOIS searches — e.g. `RegistrantContact.Organization`, `DomainName`, `NameServers`. Up to 4 search terms with optional exact-match and exclude flags, combined with AND. Use this when you need precision (search only the registrant org, not the full record). Do NOT use this for free-text searches (use `reverse_whois`) or when you have only the domain (use `whois`).

count_only.description: If true, returns only count (no credit usage). If false, returns domain list.

created_date_from.description: Search domains created after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

created_date_to.description: Search domains created before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

expired_date_from.description: Search domains that expired after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

expired_date_to.description: Search domains that expired before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

include_audit_dates.description: If true, includes domain list and last audit date.

punycode.description: If true, encodes domain names to Punycode.

search_after.description: Pagination needle from previous page's "nextPageSearchAfter" value.

search_terms.description: Field-specific WHOIS search term objects (max 4), combined with AND. Each object has "field" (required) and "term" (required), plus optional "exclude" and "exact_match" booleans. A JSON-encoded string of the same array is also accepted for backward compatibility.

exact_match.description: If true, exact field match instead of substring.

exclude.description: If true, exclude matching records from results.

field.description: WHOIS field to search, e.g. DomainName, RegistrarName, NameServers, Email, RegistrantContact.Organization.

term.description: Search string. Case insensitive, supports wildcards.

search_type.description: Search type: "current" or "historic". "current" searches current records, "historic" searches all records.

updated_date_from.description: Search domains updated after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

updated_date_to.description: Search domains updated before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: ssl_certificates
tools.description: Retrieve TLS certificate details for a domain — issuer, validity period, subject alternative names (SANs), chain trust status. Optionally returns the full chain. Use this when investigating SAN-based pivots (other domains on the same cert), expired/self-signed cert posture, or CT-log evidence of recent issuance. Do NOT use this to enumerate subdomains directly (use `subdomain_lookup`); SANs are a side effect, not the primary signal.

domain.description: The domain name to check TLS certificate for (e.g., example.com)

include_chain.description: Whether to include the full certificate chain in the response; defaults to false

use_fresh_data.description: Whether to get fresh data instead of cached results; defaults to false

tools.name: subdomain_lookup
tools.description: Enumerate the known subdomains of a single domain, with first-/last-seen timestamps per subdomain. Use this for attack-surface mapping on a target organisation's apex domain. Can return tens of thousands of rows, so it is paginated: keep calling with "next_page_token" copied from the previous response for as long as "has_more" is true, and you will walk the whole set — including past the upstream's 10000-per-request cap. "total_count" counts the rows currently fetched, NOT the size of the whole result set: the upstream offers no total, so the only way to know it is to page to the end. Do NOT use this for searching domains or subdomains by name pattern (use `domain_and_subdomain_discovery`) or for processing many apex domains at once (use `bulk_subdomain_lookup`).

domain_name.description: Domain name to lookup subdomains for.

limit.description: Number of results to return (1-500, default 500). Ignored when "next_page_token" is supplied: a continuation keeps the page size the walk started with, so change it only on the first call.

next_page_token.description: IMPORTANT: To fetch the next page, copy the "next_page_token" value from the previous response and pass it here. Do not use "search_after" or any other parameter name - only "next_page_token" is accepted.

tools.name: threat_intelligence
tools.description: Check whether an indicator (domain, URL, IP, CIDR, or file hash) appears in known malware, phishing, spam, or botnet feeds. Returns `total` (all matching records, not capped by `limit`) and `results`, one record per match: `value` (the matched indicator), `iocType` (IPv4, IPv6, URL, domain, hash, or CIDR), `threatType` (attack, botnet, C&C, malware, phishing, spam, suspicious, tor, or generic), and `firstSeen`/`lastSeen` dates. An empty `results` list means no feed record matched, not that the indicator is safe. Use this on every suspicious indicator before deeper enrichment — it's the cheapest gate. Do NOT use this for content-category labels like "gambling" or "adult" (use `categorization`) or for typosquat detection (use `typosquatting`).

limit.description: Maximum records per page. Max: 10,000. Every 100 records = 1 credit.

search_term.description: IoC to check: domain, URL, IP, CIDR, or hash. Supports wildcards for domains, URLs, IPs.

tools.name: typosquatting
tools.description: Check whether a domain belongs to a typosquatting group, or expand every domain across all groups containing it. Use `mode=probe` for a fast inGroup boolean + groupId triage. Use `mode=group` to enumerate the full lookalike infrastructure once a probe hits. Do NOT use this to find impersonation domains or subdomains by name pattern (use `domain_and_subdomain_discovery`) or for malware/phishing reputation (use `threat_intelligence`).

mode.description: Response shape: "probe" for boolean + groupId only (fast); "group" for full list of domains across all groups (heavier, more credits).

tools.name: vpn_proxy_detection
tools.description: Check whether one IP address belongs to a known VPN, proxy (including residential and open proxies), Tor exit, relay, hosting or CDN network. Every plan returns classification (for example vpn, proxy, tor, hosting, cdn or unknown), risk_score (0-100), is_vpn / is_proxy / is_tor and related flags, ASN and reason codes. provider and netblock owner need Starter or higher; confidence, seen times and residential-proxy network names need Pro or higher, null below. A residential-proxy network is named only where its exit is attributed. Data is IPv4-first; IPv6 mostly returns unknown. Reserved and private addresses are rejected. Costs 1 VPN & Proxy Detection API credit per successful lookup. Use this to vet the IP behind a login, signup or API call. Do NOT use this for location data (use `ipgeolocation`) or for 2 or more IPs (use `bulk_vpn_proxy_detection`).

ip_address.description: IP address to classify (e.g., 185.220.101.1). IPv4 recommended; see the tool description for IPv6.

tools.name: website_screenshot
tools.description: Capture a screenshot of a web page for a URL and return it as a native image content block plus a base64-encoded JSON payload (JSON's base64 field is deprecated as of 2026-10-04; prefer the native image block). Choose the output format with the type parameter: "png" (default) or "jpg" for raster images, or "pdf" to render the page as a PDF. Optionally set the viewport width and height in pixels, and enable full-page capture to grab the entire scrollable page instead of just the visible viewport. Use this to obtain visual evidence of how a site actually looks — for example to document a suspicious, phishing, or typosquatting page surfaced by another tool. Do NOT use it to read a page's text, fetch DNS or WHOIS records, or classify the site, since those have their own tools.

full_page.description: If true, capture the full scrollable page rather than just the viewport.

height.description: Viewport height in pixels. Optional; the API uses a default when omitted.

type.description: Output format of the screenshot: "png" (default) or "jpg" for raster images, or "pdf" for a PDF rendering.

url.description: The fully-qualified URL of the page to capture (e.g., https://example.com).

width.description: Viewport width in pixels. Optional; the API uses a default when omitted.

tools.name: whois
tools.description: Look up current WHOIS / RDAP registration data for a single domain — registrar, creation/expiry/updated dates, nameservers, status codes, and contact info when not redacted. Use this as the first move when triaging an unknown or suspicious domain. Do NOT use this when you need historical ownership changes (use `whois_history`) or when you have many domains in a list (use `bulk_whois`).

fetch_whois_from_registry_only.description: If true, returns only registry WHOIS data, not registrar data.

force_refresh.description: If true, forces hard refresh. Costs 5 API calls.

get_host_ip_whois_on_no_domain_data.description: If true, returns host IP WHOIS when domain WHOIS is unavailable.

get_registrar_proxy_data.description: If true, includes registrar WHOIS proxy info in "privateWhoisProxy".

include_domain_availability.description: If true, includes domain availability status.

include_ip_for_domain_queried.description: If true, includes hosting IP address for the domain.

parse_registrar_raw_text.description: If true, provides parsed format for registrar information.

parse_registry_raw_text.description: If true, provides parsed format for registry information.

prefer_refresh_even_if_incomplete.description: If true, provides most up-to-date but potentially incomplete data.

query_type.description: Query type: "auto", "whois", or "rdap". "rdap" is only supported in domain queries but might not be available for all domains. "auto" will always choose correctly.

remove_raw_text.description: If true, removes raw text from WHOIS output.

tools.name: whois_history
tools.description: Retrieve the full timeline of WHOIS changes for a domain — ownership transfers, registrar moves, nameserver swaps, and contact edits over time. Use this when investigating attribution, domain age, or whether a domain recently changed hands (a common phishing precursor). Do NOT use this for current registration only (use `whois`) or for enriched-but-current data (use `domain_info`).

created_date_from.description: Search domains created after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

created_date_to.description: Search domains created before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

expired_date_from.description: Search domains expired after this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.

expired_date_to.description: Search domains expired before this date. Format: YYYY-MM-DD.
